facts.fact: It is a castle-like eclectic building set within the Maschpark.

facts.fact: Architects Hermann Eggert and Gustav Halmhuber built it on 6,026 beech piles for 10 million marks.
facts.quote: Costing 10 million marks, the New Town Hall was erected on 6,026 beech piles by architects Hermann Eggert and Gustav Halmhuber.

facts.fact: Lower Saxony was proclaimed in its 38-metre-high hall in 1946.
facts.quote: Damaged during bombing raids on the inner city of Hanover in World War II, the German state of Lower Saxony was proclaimed in 1946 in the 38-metre-high (125 ft) hall of the New Town Hall.

facts.fact: Four city models on the ground floor show Hanover's development.
facts.quote: There are four city models of Hanover in the ground floor of the New Town Hall.

facts.fact: The dome's lift is unique because its arched course follows the dome's parabolic shape.
facts.quote: The dome's lift is unique in the world in that its arched course follows the parabolic shape of the dome.

facts.fact: The lift climbs at up to 17° to a gallery with views to the Harz mountains in good visibility.
facts.quote: The lift climbs the 50-metre (160 ft) shaft at an angle of up to 17° to the gallery of the dome, where the Harz mountain range can be seen when visibility is good.

facts.fact: It is a convention center in Osaka, also known as Grand Cube Osaka.

facts.quote: Located adjacent to the convention center is underground Nakanoshima Station served by Keihan Electric Railway Nakanoshima Line as the terminus.

facts.fact: Karl Friedrich Schinkel's plans were built between 1825 and 1830 for King Frederick William III; it is considered a major work of German Neoclassical architecture.
facts.quote: Built between 1825 and 1830 by order of King Frederick William III of Prussia according to plans by Karl Friedrich Schinkel, it is considered a major work of German Neoclassical architecture.

facts.fact: The king charged Schinkel with planning a public museum for the royal art collection.
facts.quote: King Friedrich Wilhelm III of Prussia was a strong proponent of this Humboldtian ideal for education and charged Karl Friedrich Schinkel with planning a public museum for the royal art collection.

facts.fact: The crown prince, who wanted a building heavily influenced by classical antiquity, shaped the plans.
facts.quote: Schinkel's plans for the Königliches Museum, as it was then known, were also influenced by drafts of the crown prince, the future King Friedrich Wilhelm IV, who desired a building that was heavily influenced by Classical antiquity.

facts.fact: Schinkel placed the museum in an ensemble around the Lustgarten with the palace, arsenal and cathedral.
facts.quote: The Stadtschloss in the south was a symbol of worldly power, the Zeughaus in the west represented military might, and the Berliner Dom in the east was the embodiment of divine authority.

facts.fact: The museum stood for science and art and the educated middle class.
facts.quote: The museum to the north of the garden, which was to provide for the education of the people, stood as a symbol for science and art—and not least for their torchbearer: the self-aware bourgeoisie.

facts.fact: A simple columned hall in grand style was planned for the front facing the Lustgarten.
facts.quote: For the front facing the Lustgarten, a simple columned hall in grand style and proportionate to the importance of the location would most certainly give the building character.

facts.fact: Plans date from 1822/23 but construction began only in 1825.
facts.quote: Schinkel had developed plans for the Königliches Museum as early as 1822/23, but construction did not begin until 1825.

facts.fact: It was renamed the Altes Museum in 1845, when the Neues Museum was completed.
facts.quote: In 1845, with the completion of the Neues Museum ("New"), the Königliches Museum was renamed the Altes Museum ("Old"), a name it holds to this day.

facts.fact: It is part of the Museum Island UNESCO World Heritage Site, listed in 1999.
facts.quote: As part of the Museum Island complex, the Altes Museum was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1999, in recognition of its testimony to the development of the museum as a social and architectural phenomenon.

facts.fact: It was built between 1965 and 1976 on a 35-acre site.
facts.quote: The estate was built between 1965 and 1976, on a 35-acre (14 ha) site.

facts.fact: Chamberlin, Powell and Bon designed it; their first work was the Golden Lane Estate just north.
facts.quote: The complex was designed by architects Chamberlin, Powell and Bon, whose first work was the ground-breaking Golden Lane Estate immediately north of the Barbican.

facts.fact: Unlike Golden Lane, it was not social housing.
facts.quote: Unlike its northern neighbour, however, the Barbican Estate was not social housing.

facts.fact: Concrete is the visible face of the flats, reflecting widespread 1960s and 1970s British practice.
facts.quote: The flats reflect the widespread use in Britain in the 1960s and 1970s of concrete as the visible face of the building.

facts.fact: Vehicles are completely separated from pedestrians ('slab urbanism').
facts.quote: The complex is also characterised by its total separation of vehicles from pedestrians throughout the area ("slab urbanism").

facts.fact: Pedestrians use 'highwalks' one to three storeys above the ground.
facts.quote: This is achieved through the use of 'highwalks'—walkways of varying width and shape, usually 1 to 3 storeys above the surrounding ground level.

facts.fact: The main buildings rise up to seven floors above a podium that links all the facilities.
facts.quote: The main buildings rise up to seven floors above a podium level, which links all the facilities in the Barbican, providing a pedestrian route above street level.

facts.fact: The terrace blocks are grouped around a lake and green squares.
facts.quote: The terrace blocks are grouped around a lake and green squares.

facts.fact: Three towers are 42 storeys and 123 metres high.
facts.quote: The estate also contains three of London's tallest residential towers, at 42 storeys and 123 metres (404 ft) high.

facts.fact: It was Grade II listed after a 2001 announcement.
facts.quote: The Minister for the Arts, Tessa Blackstone, announced in September 2001 that the Barbican complex was to be Grade II listed.

facts.fact: Kallmann McKinnell & Knowles and Campbell, Aldrich & Nulty designed it, with LeMessurier Consultants as engineers.
facts.quote: The building was designed by the architecture firms Kallmann McKinnell & Knowles (KMK) and Campbell, Aldrich & Nulty, with LeMessurier Consultants as engineers.

facts.fact: It was proposed in 1956 as part of the Government Center development.
facts.quote: City Hall was proposed in 1956 as part of the Government Center development, following decades of efforts to replace Old City Hall.

facts.fact: KMK won a two-phase design competition in 1962.
facts.quote: Acquiring the land and sufficient funding took half a decade, and KMK won a two-phase architectural design competition in 1962.

facts.fact: The nine-storey mass is split into three tiers matching the interior subdivisions.
facts.quote: The nine-story massing is split into three tiers, corresponding to the interior subdivisions.

facts.fact: Public areas are on floors one to four, elected officials on five, and nonpublic agencies on six to nine.
facts.quote: There are public areas on the first through fourth stories, elected officials' spaces on the fifth story, and nonpublic agencies at the sixth through ninth stories.

facts.fact: The facade is brick below and concrete above.
facts.quote: The facade is made of brick below and concrete above, with entrances on the bottom three levels.

facts.fact: Hoods project around the fifth-floor windows and the upper floors protrude around a central courtyard.
facts.quote: There are protruding "hoods" around the fifth-floor windows, while the upper stories protrude outward, surrounding a central fourth-story courtyard.

facts.fact: The entrance vestibule leads down a ramp to a small lobby with a coffered concrete ceiling with Vierendeel trusses.
facts.quote: These spaces have concrete walls and a coffered concrete ceiling with Vierendeel trusses.

facts.fact: It received the AIA's 1969 Honor Award, but the public widely condemned it.
facts.quote: City Hall received the American Institute of Architects' 1969 Honor Award and was ranked in a 1976 poll of the United States' greatest buildings.

facts.fact: It has influenced Brutalist architecture in Boston and elsewhere.
facts.quote: The design has influenced Brutalist architecture in Boston, along with similar buildings across the U.S. and worldwide.

facts.fact: Frank Gehry designed it with structural engineering by Skidmore, Owings and Merrill; it opened on 16 July 2004.
facts.quote: Designed by Pritzker Prize-winning architect Frank Gehry and structurally engineered by Skidmore, Owings and Merrill, it opened along with the rest of Millennium Park on July 16, 2004.

facts.fact: It spans Columbus Drive, linking Maggie Daley Park with Millennium Park.
facts.quote: It spans Columbus Drive to connect Maggie Daley Park (formerly, Daley Bicentennial Plaza) with Millennium Park, both parts of the larger Grant Park.

facts.fact: It is the first Gehry-designed bridge completed.
facts.quote: Named for energy firm BP, which donated $5 million toward its construction, it is the first Gehry-designed bridge to have been completed.

facts.fact: It is described as snakelike because of its curving form.
facts.quote: BP Bridge is described as snakelike because of its curving form.

facts.fact: It has won awards for its use of sheet metal.
facts.quote: Designed to bear a heavy load without structural problems caused by its own weight, it has won awards for its use of sheet metal.

facts.fact: It uses a concealed box girder with a concrete base and a hardwood deck.
facts.quote: BP Bridge uses a concealed box girder design with a concrete base, and its deck is covered by hardwood floor boards.

facts.fact: It has no handrails; stainless steel parapets are used instead.
facts.quote: It is designed without handrails, using stainless steel parapets instead.

facts.fact: It is 935 feet long with a five percent slope, making it accessible.
facts.quote: The total length is 935 feet (285 m), with a five percent slope on its inclined surfaces that makes it barrier free and accessible.

facts.fact: It acts as a noise barrier against traffic on Columbus Drive.
facts.quote: The pedestrian bridge serves as a noise barrier for traffic sounds from Columbus Drive.

facts.fact: It is closed in winter because ice cannot be safely removed from the wooden walkway.
facts.quote: Although the bridge is closed in winter because ice cannot be safely removed from its wooden walkway, it has received favorable reviews for its design and aesthetics.

facts.fact: A 1909 law mandated a direct connection between the Brussels stations, but it took nearly half a century to complete.
facts.quote: A law was finally passed in 1909 mandating a direct connection; however, the final project would not be completed until nearly half a century later.

facts.fact: Victor Horta was awarded the design in 1910.
facts.quote: The famed architect Victor Horta was awarded the design of the Central Station building complex in 1910.

facts.fact: The original plans were part of a major urban redevelopment; over 1,000 buildings were demolished in the 1920s.
facts.quote: Plans for the station originally featured a major urban redevelopment project, for which land was purchased and over 1,000 buildings demolished in the 1920s.

facts.fact: World War II slowed construction again.
facts.quote: However, World War II slowed construction again.

facts.fact: After Horta's death in 1947, a team led by Maxime Brunfaut took over construction.
facts.quote: Following his death, in 1947, an architectural team led by Maxime Brunfaut, son of the architect Fernand Brunfaut, president of the National Bureau of the North–South connection, was entrusted with the station's construction.

facts.fact: Brunfaut finished it to Horta's plans, adding an airport line and underground pedestrian passages.
facts.quote: The building was completed according to Horta's plans by Brunfaut, who expanded them by adding a new train line to Brussels Airport, in the suburb of Zaventem, as well as several underground passageways for pedestrians.

facts.fact: It was inaugurated on 4 October 1952.
facts.quote: The station was finally inaugurated on 4 October 1952.

facts.fact: Six tracks are served by three underground island platforms.
facts.quote: Brussels Central Station has six tracks, served by three island platforms.

facts.fact: The main entrance and ticket office are at ground level on the Boulevard de l'Impératrice.
facts.quote: The main entrance and ticket office are at ground level on the Boulevard de l'Impératrice, and there are several other entrances on the other streets.

facts.fact: It is an Olympic-standard multi-use stadium with an all-seated capacity of 75,000.
facts.quote: is an Olympic-standard, multi-use stadium with an all-seated capacity of 75,000.

facts.fact: German architect Werner March, who designed Berlin's Olympic Stadium, designed it.
facts.quote: The architect of the stadium is the German Werner March, who designed the Olympic Stadium in Berlin from 1934 to 1936.

facts.fact: Moharram Bakhoum supervised the engineering and construction.
facts.quote: The engineering and construction supervision of the stadium was performed by ACE Moharram Bakhoum.

facts.fact: It is a symbol of Egyptian football and hosts nearly all the most important Egyptian matches.
facts.quote: Nearly all of the most important Egyptian matches are held there.

facts.fact: It hosted the 2009 FIFA U-20 World Cup final between Brazil and Ghana.
facts.quote: Several matches of the 2009 FIFA U-20 World Cup were played at the stadium, including the two semifinals, the third-place match, and the final between Brazil and Ghana.

facts.fact: It was a venue for the 2019 Africa Cup of Nations.
facts.quote: The stadium was one of the venues for the 2019 Africa Cup of Nations.

facts.fact: It is about 10 km from downtown Cairo.
facts.quote: The stadium is located about 10 km west of Cairo International Airport and about 10 km from downtown Cairo.

facts.fact: It can be reached by Cairo metro line 3 via a dedicated stadium station.
facts.quote: can be reached by underground via the dedicated Cairo stadium subway station at line 3

facts.fact: Construction started in March 2008 and finished in 2015.
facts.quote: Its construction started in March 2008 and was completed in 2015.

facts.fact: It is the tallest building in Andalusia and Seville.
facts.quote: The tower is the tallest building in Andalusia and in the city of Seville, and the eighth tallest in Spain.

facts.fact: It stands in La Cartuja, the site of the 1992 Universal Exposition.
facts.quote: The tower is located in La Cartuja, the former zone of the Universal Exposition that took place in Seville between April and October 1992.

facts.fact: Two four-storey podium buildings, also by César Pelli, flank the tower.
facts.quote: The tower is flanked by two four story podium buildings also designed by César Pelli.

facts.fact: The podiums' curved edges form a plaza that narrows at the centre into a pedestrian-scaled commercial street.
facts.quote: The curved edges of the podium buildings define a plaza that opens on the north and south and narrows at the center, creating a pedestrian-scaled commercial street.

facts.fact: The competition brief asked for a new icon for the city, preferably one single high-rise.
facts.quote: The main requirement was that the building should be a new icon for the city and, "preferably," should concentrate the building's volume into a single high-rise structure.

facts.fact: An earlier scheme hired Ricardo Bofill, who proposed a glass tower.
facts.quote: The investors hired the Catalan architect Ricardo Bofill Leví for the project, who proposed a glass tower.

facts.fact: It has LEED Gold certification.
facts.quote: The building also obtained LEED Gold certification from the U.S. Green Building Council.

facts.fact: RMJM designed it and it was completed in 2011.
facts.quote: Capital Gate was designed by architectural firm RMJM and was completed in 2011.

facts.fact: It was designed to incline 18° west, more than three times the lean of the Leaning Tower of Pisa.
facts.quote: Capital Gate is one of the tallest buildings in the city and was designed to incline 18° west, more than three times the lean of the Leaning Tower of Pisa.

facts.fact: It rests on 490 pilings drilled 30 metres below ground.
facts.quote: The structure rests on a foundation of 490 pilings that have been drilled 30 meters (98 ft) below ground.

facts.fact: The pilings resist wind, gravity and seismic pressures caused by the incline.
facts.quote: The deep pilings provide stability against strong winds, gravitational pull, and seismic pressures that arise due to the incline of the building.

facts.fact: The core was built with a slight opposite lean (pre-camber).
facts.quote: This pre-camber means the core was constructed with a slight opposite lean.

facts.fact: The weight of the floors and diagrid slowly pulled the core straight as each floor was added.
facts.quote: As each floor was installed, the weight of the floors and diagonal grid, or diagrid, system pulled the core and slowly straightened it out.

facts.fact: Two diagrid systems were needed: an external one shaping the tower and an internal one linked to the core.
facts.quote: Given the 18° lean of the building, the construction required two diagrid systems: an external diagrid defining the tower's shape and an internal diagrid linked to the central core by eight unique, pin-jointed structural members.

facts.fact: The diagrids carry floor loads to the core, so floors need no columns.
facts.quote: The external grid carries the weight of the floor while the internal diagrid connects with the external and transfers the load to the core, thereby eliminating the need for columns in the floor.

facts.fact: The tower has office space and the Andaz Hotel on floors 18 to 33.
facts.quote: The tower includes 16,000 square meters (170,000 sq ft) of office space and the Andaz Hotel on floors 18 through 33.

facts.fact: It houses a museum of contemporary art and the municipal library in Nîmes.
facts.quote: The Carré d'art at Nîmes in southern France houses a museum of contemporary art and the city's municipal library.

facts.fact: It is glass, concrete and steel and faces the Roman Maison carrée.
facts.quote: Constructed of glass, concrete and steel, it faces the Maison carrée, a perfectly preserved Roman temple that dates from the very beginning of the 1st century AD.

facts.fact: Twelve architects were invited to propose in 1984; Norman Foster's design was chosen.
facts.quote: A design by the British architect Norman Foster was selected, and the building was opened in May 1993.

facts.fact: It was built as part of refurbishing the square, giving the ancient temple a new setting.
facts.quote: The building was constructed as part of a project to refurbish the square in which the Maison carrée stands, and provides a new setting for the ancient temple.

facts.fact: Half of its nine storeys are sunk into the ground to keep the profile low.
facts.quote: The building is a nine-storey structure, half of which is sunk deep into the ground, keeping the building's profile low in sympathy with the scale of the surrounding buildings.

facts.fact: The lower levels hold archival storage and a cinema.
facts.quote: The lower levels house archival storage and a cinema.

facts.fact: The Roman theatre was built between 5 and 1 BCE and held about 6,000 spectators.
facts.quote: Built between the years 5 and 1 BCE, it had a capacity of some 6,000 spectators and was used for Roman theatrical performances.

facts.fact: It sits in the slope of a hill, with stands facing north and protected from easterly winds.
facts.quote: Nevertheless, the romans thought about the selection of this urban area near the port; on the one hand the building was far from the unhealthy area of the lagoon, located at the other end of the city, on the other hand it took advantage of the morphography of the land, locating it in the slope of the hill, built into the natural terrain, to fit the stands facing north and protected from the prevailing easterly winds.

facts.fact: Its axis points to the sunrise at the winter solstice.
facts.quote: Its astronomical orientation was also taken into account, so that the axial axis of the building is directed to the sunrise at the winter solstice.

facts.fact: Rafael Moneo was awarded the restoration project in 2003, after more than 10 years of excavation.
facts.quote: After more than 10 years of excavation projects to bring the 1st century BC Roman Theater to light, the restoration project was awarded to the architect Rafael Moneo in 2003.

facts.fact: Moneo worked with archaeologists and a restoration specialist to consolidate the ruins.
facts.quote: To this end, Moneo worked with archaeologists Sebastián Ramallo and Elena Ruiz and the restoration specialist Isabel García-Galán in consolidating the theatre's ruins.

facts.fact: The project integrates with nearby buildings, including the Old Cathedral partly built over the theatre's grandstand.
facts.quote: He tries to integrate the project with different historical buildings in the area, with a particular emphasis on the unique partial superimposition of the so-called Old Cathedral (Santa María la Vieja) on part of the Theater's grandstand, as well as parts of the Roman house prior to the Theater, which are still preserved inside the museum.

facts.fact: Its recovery became the engine of regeneration of a large part of the old town.
facts.quote: Over time it had become one of the most depressed and abandoned areas of the old town, so that the comprehensive recovery of the Roman building has transcended a simple archaeological investigation and has become the engine of regeneration of a large sector of the city.

facts.fact: Rem Koolhaas and Ole Scheeren of OMA were the architects, with Cecil Balmond at Arup as engineer.
facts.quote: Rem Koolhaas and Ole Scheeren of OMA were the architects in charge for the building, while Cecil Balmond at Arup provided the complex engineering design.

facts.fact: OMA won the contract in 2002 after an international design competition.
facts.quote: The Office for Metropolitan Architecture won the contract from the Beijing International Tendering Co. to construct the CCTV Headquarters and the Television Cultural Center by its side on 1 January 2002, after winning an international design competition.

facts.fact: It is a loop of six horizontal and vertical sections around an open centre, not a traditional tower.
facts.quote: The main building is not a traditional tower, but a loop of six horizontal and vertical sections covering 473,000 m2 (5,090,000 sq ft) of floor space, creating an irregular grid on the building's façade with an open center.

facts.fact: The loop is intended to symbolize collectivity, communication, continuity and integration.
facts.quote: The loop of its design is intended to symbolize concepts of collectivity, communication, continuity, and integration.

facts.fact: The structure is a challenge because it is in a seismic zone.
facts.quote: The construction of the building is considered to be a structural challenge, especially because it is in a seismic zone.

facts.fact: The two towers were joined in the early morning, when their steel was at the same temperature.
facts.quote: In order not to lock in structural differentials, this connection was scheduled in the early morning when the steel in the two towers cooled to the same temperature.

facts.fact: It was part of a planned media park.
facts.quote: The CCTV building was part of a media park intended to form a landscape of public entertainment, outdoor filming areas, and production studios as an extension of the central green axis of the CBD.

facts.fact: Construction began in June 2004 and the facade was completed in January 2008.
facts.quote: The building's construction began on 1 June 2004 and its façade was completed in January 2008.

facts.fact: It was named 2013 Best Tall Building Worldwide by the CTBUH.
facts.quote: The structure was feted by some architectural critics as "the greatest work of architecture built in this century" and was named the 2013 Best Tall Building Worldwide by the Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat.
